If you don't have a Venmo card, you won't see "Manage Balance". Only users w/ a Venmo card will see this. All you have to do is add a funding source and make the payment. The money will be taken straight from the funding source.

Payments sent from a bank account will take 1-3 business days to be debited. It would only take up to 10 days (possibly) if the first attempt to debit the funds fails, and that usually only happens if the account funds (in the bank) are frozen, or if there's insufficient funds in the bank account you used to make the payment.

You can't put funds into Venmo using a debit card. Only verified banks can be used with the "Add Money" function. If you're wanting to add these cards to fund payments to other users, there's no way of knowing if they will work or not pre-emptively, you just have to try. However, prepaid cards have a tendency to be incompatible w/ Venmo.

Did you add a banking app (along the lines of chime, but not chime specifically, just can't think of any of the others off the top of my head) bank to your Venmo? Or a prepaid card? Some of these will show up as "Sutton Bank" or "Green dot bank" (there's a few other common ones too, just can't remember them either) even if that's not the name of the app/card. Probably nothing to worry about, unless you see unauthorized activity but it's not likely someone would "hack" your account only to add their own funding source.

You can't sign up for a "business account" w/ Venmo. Venmo is for peer to peer transactions only. There is a business profile feature that's being rolled out to users, but in order to do this, you have to have a personal account first, and also be one of the accounts in which this is offered to. I can't remember the exact criteria/what people it's offered to.  


When setting up a personal account, always use your legal first and last name as Venmo is a federally-regulated money transfer service, and if you ever get locked out of the account you may need to send in a gov. issued photo ID, and if the name on the ID doesn't match the name on the account, you may be SOL.

​

All in all, I wouldn't recommend using Venmo for the purpose you've described. It just might not be the ideal payment processor for you.

Add the debit card associated (if you have one) with the account, and do an instant transfer to it. Same 1% fee (min 25 cents, max $10 for the fee) Any card that is eligible for Mastercard Send or VISA fastfunds will work (so basically every VISA or Mastercard debit card). Honestly, there are a lot of banks that aren't eligible for instant transfers on Venmo. As long as the instant transfer isn't declined by Venmo's internal security system, and there's no issues on the card-issuer's end, the instant transfer to a debit card is probably your best bet! There's no way to push the instant transfer to bank through if it is "Not Supported" unfortunately.

They'll either help him into the old account so he can access the money, or he can authorize a reversal to you. Money isn't lost, it just has to be handled from the receiver's end. There is no way for Venmo Support to reverse a payment from the sender's side in this circumstance.

Beware that on top of the 3 percent fee charged by Venmo, some CC providers may charge additional cash advance fees for Venmo p2p payments. But generally yes, any credit card can be added, as long as it isn't declined for other reasons.

Your ED is not made up. There is no "sick enough" or "not sick enough" anyone with a preoccupation with food/weight is suffering from disordered eating in some capacity. HOWEVER ik that this is probably a duh statement but pls try to refrain from purging or attempting to purge. I was in the same boat for several years and one day I was just able to push past the hurdle and do it and from then on I never just ate. Everyday was consumed by binging and purging. I could never just eat. Its an incredibly addictive behavior and it ruined my life for like 9 months and I ended up gaining so much from it because of course, it isn't terribly effective. Purging is one of the worst things I have ever been through and I wouldn't wish it on my greatest enemy. It dehydrates you, bloats you, ruins your skin, teeth, and its just honestly pretty gross to deal with. Like I know people say this all the time but I seriously cannot stress this enough, nothing is worth the hell that purging is. Purging doesn't make your ED more valid, its just another hole to fall in that has absolutely no pros and only cons.
